title: Por vs. para
summary: Two words for 'for'. Para aims at a goal. Por gives the cause, route, price or means.
content:
## Para: aiming at something

**Para** points forward, at a goal. Think of an arrow pointing *towards* something.

| use | example |
|---|---|
| purpose (in order to) | **Estudio español para trabajar en España.** I study Spanish to work in Spain. |
| destination | **Este tren va para Sevilla.** This train is heading for Seville. |
| deadline | **El informe es para el lunes.** The report is for Monday. |
| recipient | **Este regalo es para ti.** This present is for you. |
| opinion | **Para mí, es la mejor playa.** For me, it's the best beach. |
| employer | **Trabajo para una empresa alemana.** I work for a German company. |

**¿Para qué?** asks *what for?* For example, **¿Para qué sirve esto?** (What is this for?)

## Por: the reason and the route

**Por** looks backward at the cause, or sideways at the way something happens.

| use | example |
|---|---|
| cause, motive | **Cerraron por la lluvia.** They closed because of the rain. |
| thanks and apologies | **Gracias por tu ayuda.** Thanks for your help. |
| through, along, around | **Paseamos por el parque.** We stroll through the park. |
| exchange, price | **Lo compré por diez euros.** I bought it for ten euros. |
| means | **Hablamos por teléfono.** We talk on the phone. |
| duration | **Viví allí por dos años.** I lived there for two years. (*durante* is more common) |
| part of the day | **Por la mañana trabajo.** In the morning I work. |

**¿Por qué?** asks *why?* It asks for the reason behind.

## Same sentence, two meanings

The choice changes the meaning:

- **Lo hago por ti.** I do it because of you (you are the reason).
- **Lo hago para ti.** I do it for you (you receive it).
- **Voy por Madrid.** I go via Madrid.
- **Voy para Madrid.** I'm heading to Madrid.
- **Trabajo por mi hermano.** I'm working instead of my brother.
- **Trabajo para mi hermano.** I work for my brother (he's my boss).

Rule of thumb: if you can say *in order to*, *destined for* or *by (a deadline)*, it's **para**. If you can say *because of*, *through*, *in exchange for* or *by means of*, it's **por**.

## Fixed phrases

Some expressions are learnt as whole units. Most take **por**:

- **por favor**: please
- **por ejemplo**: for example
- **por fin**: at last
- **por supuesto**: of course
- **por lo menos**: at least
- **por eso**: that's why
- **por cierto**: by the way

A few take **para**:

- **para siempre**: forever
- **para nada**: not at all
- **para variar**: for a change

vocabulary.example: Me gustan las frutas, por ejemplo las fresas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I like fruit, for example strawberries.
Can you help me? Of course.

vocabulary.example: Duerme por lo menos siete horas.

vocabulary.example_meaning: It's raining; that's why we're not going out.
I want to live here forever.

vocabulary.example: Hablamos por teléfono todos los días.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We talk on the phone every day.
I work for a German company.

vocabulary.meaning: to go for a walk, to stroll

vocabulary.example: El informe es para el lunes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The report is due on Monday.

quiz.explanation: The person who receives something is introduced by para: 'es para ti'.
hints: Who gets the present? Recipient Recipient takes para.

quiz.explanation: Purpose ('in order to') takes para + infinitive: 'para trabajar'.

quiz.prompt: Paseamos ___ el parque todas las tardes.
quiz.explanation: Movement through or around a place is por: 'por el parque'. Para would mean the park is the destination.
Thanks and apologies take por, because the help is the reason for the thanks.
hints: Thanks are given for a reason. Which of the two marks a cause?

quiz.explanation: A deadline is a point you aim at, so it takes para: 'para el lunes'.
hints: By when? Deadline Recipient takes para.

quiz.explanation: Your employer takes para: 'trabajo para una empresa'. Por would mean you are standing in for someone.
hints: The company is the one you work for.

quiz.explanation: A price or exchange takes por: 'por diez euros'.
hints: Money changes hands. An exchange takes por.

quiz.explanation: The means of communication takes por: 'por teléfono', 'por correo', 'por internet'.
hints: By what means? Means take the same preposition as causes.

quiz.prompt: ___ mí, esta ciudad es la mejor de España.
quiz.explanation: An opinion is introduced with para: 'para mí' (in my view). 'Por mí' means 'as far as I'm concerned / I don't mind'.
hints: In my opinion takes para mí.

listening.text: Este regalo es para mi madre.
listening.meaning: This present is for my mother.
What do you need the report for today?

listening.text: Por la tarde paseamos por el río.
listening.meaning: In the afternoon we stroll along the river.
listening.note: New word: el río = the river.

listening.text: Mi hermana trabaja para una empresa de Madrid.
listening.meaning: My sister works for a company in Madrid.

listening.text: No tengo trabajo, por eso estudio inglés para encontrar uno.
listening.meaning: I don't have a job, that's why I'm studying English to find one.

listening.text: Hablé con mi abuela por teléfono por lo menos una hora.
listening.meaning: I talked to my grandmother on the phone for at least an hour.

guide.tip: Para looks ahead (goal, destination, deadline, recipient). Por looks back at the cause or sideways at the route, price or means.

conversations.title: A weekend in Valencia
conversations.scenario: Marta asks Luis about his plans; he is driving to Valencia for his sister's birthday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Luis, ¿qué haces este fin de semana?
lines.meaning: Luis, what are you doing this weekend?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Voy a Valencia para ver a mi hermana. Es su cumpleaños.
lines.meaning: I'm going to Valencia to see my sister. It's her birthday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué bien! ¿Vas en tren o en coche?
lines.meaning: Nice! Are you going by train or by car?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: En coche, por la autopista. Son tres horas, por lo menos si no hay tráfico.
lines.meaning: By car, along the motorway. It's three hours, at least if there's no traffic.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Y ya tienes un regalo para ella?
lines.meaning: And do you already have a present for her?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, le compré un libro por internet. Lo conseguí por diez euros.
lines.meaning: Yes, I bought her a book online. I got it for ten euros.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Es de segunda mano. Para mí, los libros usados son los mejores.
lines.meaning: It's second-hand. For me, used books are the best.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Por cierto, ¿me compras horchata? Gracias por adelantado.
lines.meaning: By the way, will you buy me some horchata? Thanks in advance.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Por supuesto. Te la traigo el domingo por la noche.
lines.meaning: Of course. I'll bring it to you on Sunday night.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Por fin voy a probar la horchata de verdad!
lines.meaning: At last I'm going to try real horchata!

bites.title: Para looks ahead
bites.rule: Para marks the goal: purpose (para + infinitive), destination, deadline, recipient, opinion (para mí), employer.

bites.title: Por looks back and around
bites.rule: Por marks the cause (gracias por), the route (por el parque), the exchange (por diez euros), the means (por teléfono), the part of the day (por la mañana).
bites.example: Paseamos por el parque por la tarde.
bites.example_meaning: We stroll through the park in the afternoon.

bites.title: Why vs. what for
bites.rule: ¿Por qué? asks for the reason behind, and ¿Para qué? asks for the goal ahead. Lo hago por ti = because of you; lo hago para ti = for you to have.

bites.title: Learn the set phrases
bites.rule: Most fixed phrases take por: por favor, por ejemplo, por fin, por supuesto, por lo menos, por eso. A few take para: para siempre, para nada.

sorts.title: Por or para?
sorts.why: Recipient, purpose, deadline and employer take para; route, thanks, price and means take por.

sorts.title: Why does it take por?
sorts.why: Por covers four jobs: the reason behind, the way through, what is swapped, and the channel used.

sorts.title: Fixed phrases
sorts.why: Por favor, por fin, por ejemplo, por supuesto and por lo menos are fixed with por; para siempre and para nada with para.

spots.why: The recipient of something takes para.
Thanks are given for a reason: gracias por.

spots.sentence: Estudio español por trabajar en España.
spots.why: Purpose ('in order to') is para + infinitive.

spots.sentence: Paseamos para el parque cada tarde.
spots.why: Movement through or around a place takes por.
A price or exchange takes por.
The means of communication takes por: por teléfono.

builds.text: Estudio español para trabajar en España.
builds.meaning: I study Spanish to work in Spain.
